note: Every withdrawal a person can make that lives outside the tombstone table, which a restore from an older backup would otherwise undo. A restore checkpoint of profile exulanica.restore-tombstone-checkpoint/v2 carries each row this names, and replay writes each one again into the restored database, before any tombstone, by the same statement the product writes: a column kind sets the columns a withdrawal sets on a row whose withdrawal is still open, and an event kind appends the withdrawal's own row. `withdrawn` is the condition a withdrawn row meets; `carried_when` narrows it; `workspace` names the column that says which workspace a row belongs to, or null for a row no workspace owns. A condition with `of` tests a column of the row the carried row names in another table, joined on the `on` columns. An event kind's `ends` names the rows the withdrawal ends, and `order` the column that orders a chain of decisions; a column kind's `order` is the column its rows are replayed by, earliest first, so a later withdrawal's cascade finds what an earlier one already ended. `writer` names the product's own writer that writes the carried row, where a row alone is not the whole withdrawal; `continues` names the writer that continues a chain whose restored last decision the carried row cannot follow, because a decision was made after the backup. Both are names of the writers the restore command gives replay (WRITERS in exulanica/orchestration/restore.py); replay refuses, when it starts and before it writes anything, writers other than exactly the names this catalog uses (require_writers in exulanica/deletion/withdrawals.py). An event kind whose `absent` is `carry` has its row written even when the restored database holds nothing it ends, because the installation makes what it ends again after a restore (a published catalog from the image), and a row the backup lacks would otherwise come back current; without it, nothing is written for an absent end. `excluded` names every other withdrawal-shaped table or column in the schema and why it is not carried; tests/test_restore_replay_withdrawal_catalog.py fails on any the catalog neither carries nor excludes.

kinds.note: A person stopping a share of a project or an item (migration 0127), and the shares a deletion closes, whatever closed them. A share is never reopened, so a restore cannot show another person what its owner stopped sharing. First of the project kinds, earliest first, so a later deletion's cascade finds the shares an earlier stop or deletion closed already closed.

A person deleting a project item, rejecting a suggestion, or deleting the project, Companion answer or item it was drawn from (migration 0127). The update erases every revision's words and references and withdraws the items copied from it with the same instant. Earliest first and ahead of projects and Companion memory, so a later deletion's cascade finds what an earlier one ended already ended. One reached through a tombstone names it and is re-derived by it.

A person deleting a world project (migration 0127). The update erases the project's title and request digest and, by owner-rights triggers, withdraws every item still open and closes every share at the same instant. Earliest first. A workspace tombstone's deletion names its tombstone and is re-derived by it.

A workspace withdrawing one of its own looks (exulanica/world/thing_store.py): a choice naming it finds none, and its container is no longer served. The row is the whole withdrawal, and nothing else a restore could bring back serves the look again.

A workspace erasing a creature drafted from a person's words (exulanica/world/thing_store.py), beside the creature tombstone it names: its trigger deletes the creature's kind and, with its drafted plan, the plan, its recipe and every look drawn on it with their withdrawals, so a restore from an older backup loses them again, and the tombstone replayed after it purges those looks' containers. The row names the kind by its document's digest only. A look withdrawal it deletes is one the checkpoint lacks, so the look kind names it among the removals the stale check passes by.

A person withdrawing a claim they made: the retraction row, and assertion.status 'retracted', which the product's retract writes together (exulanica/epistemics/assertions.py). Retracting a name clears the place or person's display name (migration 0002), and a place-name right rests on an active naming claim (0097), so a retraction can end a right. Every row is a retraction; only a retraction of a claim a person stated (kind 'user') is carried. The other writer, a tombstone's cascade (0031), retracts reconstruction_scene_rung_is claims, which only an inference may state, and the replayed tombstone retracts them again.

An operator revoking a spending authority (migration 0124): nothing more is admitted under it, and the row is the whole revocation. The spending witness holds it as well, for a restore made without a checkpoint.
An operator revoking a workspace's spending grant, or a bound closed under one (migration 0124): nothing more is admitted under it, and the row is the whole revocation.

The host withdrawing a published character catalog for good (migration 0131): no world draws from it again, a look saved over it reads as unavailable and its containers are no longer served under it. The row is the whole withdrawal, and it names a digest whether or not this database holds the publication (0135). It is carried even when the restored database holds no publication of it, because the host's catalogs job publishes what the image carries on every start and would otherwise serve the document again; publishing a withdrawn digest records the publication and leaves it withdrawn.

A world's owner revoking a door grant (migration 0149): no outside program is asked or answers under it again, and nothing revises it. The row is the whole revocation. A restore writes it again when the restored database holds the grant, so a grant ended after a backup does not open again.

An owner ending a door grant's invites and channel credentials without ending the grant (migration 0149), as after one leaked, or a new channel credential ending the grant's last: the secret opens nothing again. Backup sets carry no door secret (EPHEMERAL_TABLES in exulanica/orchestration/installation/backup_set.py), so a restore voids every credential, as it does every browser session, and a sealed checkpoint refuses a revocation like any withdrawal.

excluded.reason: A person's identity decision (not them), which undo takes back (exulanica/identity/undo.py). A restore returns it to the backup's state like any other authored edit; it withdraws no permission and no consent.
A confirmed or revoked identity link, an identity decision undo takes back, as for identity_rejection.
The log of identity decisions, derived from them.
A decision about how a place record and an entity relate, which a later decision can reverse. It withdraws no permission and no consent.

assertion.status 'retracted' is the second row of a retraction, written again with it by the retraction kind's writer. A status a tombstone's cascade sets (migrations 0030 and 0031) is written again by the replayed tombstone.
Nothing writes consent_record.revoked_at, and nothing makes a revocation there final.
failure_class 'withdrawn' is written by the recipe withdrawal's own trigger, which replaying the withdrawal runs again.
failure_class 'withdrawn' is written by the asset withdrawal's own trigger, which replaying the withdrawal runs again.

status 'withdrawn' is written by the triggers on a picture right's stop and on a tombstone (migration 0160), which replaying the right's withdrawal and the tombstone runs again, and by a job's finish under a stop, which a request restored as running meets when it reads its pictures again under the replayed stop.

A state event with basis 'withdrawal' records a tombstone's effect on a place record and names that tombstone; every read of the record asks tombstone_blocks_place_record (migration 0063), which the replayed tombstone answers again.
Written by the cascade of a person's entity tombstone (migration 0030), which replaying the tombstone runs again.
Taking a photograph out of a saved world is an authored edit of that world, not a withdrawal of a permission or a consent; a restore returns a saved world to the backup's state like any other edit.

The durable spending ledger's chain (migration 0124). Its revocation events record revocations whose own rows are carried (spending_authority, spending_grant); a restored ledger is carried forward from the spending witness, never replayed from a checkpoint.

An operator's guest policy, ended when another replaces it, when the operator withdraws it, or by the ledger (migrations 0139 and 0155). Setting and withdrawing one are ledger steps under the witness, so a restore that loses either is reconciled, and reconciling a restore, or reauthorizing, ends every live policy: nothing a restore brings back grants until the operator sets a policy again.
